page: Microsoft Azure L32as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. The configuration provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at base frequencies up to 3.7 GHz. System architecture incorporates 256 GB of memory, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, coupled with a direct-attached 7,680 GB local NVMe SSD volume. The platform operates on Microsoft Hyper-V and does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 networking addresses.

The x86_64 host processor includes an instruction set featuring AVX-512 variants such as AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside cryptographic execution flags including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The caching hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory subsystem benchmarking shows large-block uncached read bandwidth reaching 74.7 GB/s and uncached write throughput measuring 55.71 GB/s.

Benchmark results highlight solid computational execution. The instance posted strong top-quartile performance in Geekbench single-core (2,084.0) and multi-core (17,869.0) metrics, supported by a 3,078.58 score in single-core stress-ng tests. In cryptographic evaluations, PassMark CPU encryption registered in the top 25% with 38,549.06 points. Operational benchmarks show Redis executing 44.82 million SET operations per second and small-model language inference processing 338.42 generation tokens per second.

The integrated NVMe storage tier provides dense local I/O capacity, eliminating the latency overhead associated with network-attached block storage. Multi-threaded CPU tasks demonstrate average performance tiers in broader compute benchmarks, indicating that computing density balances storage throughput rather than raw processing limits. Primary application fits include transactional NoSQL and relational database management systems, search indexing, real-time caching clusters, and high-volume ETL processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L32as_v4 is a storage-optimized instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores operating at up to 3.7 GHz, 256 GB of system memory, and an integrated 7,680 GB local NVMe SSD array. It does not include discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying processor supports AVX-512 vector extensions and VAES cryptographic acceleration, contributing to strong Geekbench scores of 2,084.0 single-core and 17,869.0 multi-core, alongside high-efficiency cryptographic operations. In real-world data processing workloads, it achieves Redis throughput of 44.82 million operations per second and 74.7 GB/s uncached memory read bandwidth. With its 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-capacity direct-attached NVMe storage, the L32as_v4 provides a dense hardware footprint suited for large transactional databases, NoSQL datastores, low-latency caching systems, and high-throughput data analytics pipelines.
